notes.1: Many candidates did not find the relevant distance of 16 m. Many candidates did not use the idea that the work done by a force of magnitude F N, acting on a block at an angle α to the direction of motion of the block, for a distance of d m is given by ‘work done = F d cos α J’. Answer: 376 J
notes.2: Few candidates made progress with this question. Answers: Tension = 4.55 N, Magnitude = 9.1 N
notes.3: Most candidates resolved forces in a given direction to find the component of the resultant in that direction. Fully correct answers for parts (i), (a) and (b) were uncommon. Part (ii) is dependent on the answers in part (i). Many candidates omitted to note that R2 = X2 + Y2 and tan θ =Y÷X. Answers: (i) (a) 8.74 N; (b) 11.5 N; (ii) 14.4 N, 52.7° to the i direction
notes.4: Most candidates were aware of the formulae for motion in a straight line with constant acceleration. Many did not develop a strategy for using these formulae effectively. Answers: (i) u = 1.4, a = 2; (ii) θ = 11.5°
notes.5: Most candidates were aware of the need to resolve forces vertically and horizontally. Many did not find R = 27.2 in (i) or R = 12.8 in (ii), or F = 9.6 in (i) and (ii), where R N and F N are the normal and frictional forces acting on the block. Answer: (ii) μ < 3/4
notes.6: In part (i) there is no change in speed and hence no change in kinetic energy. The car moves uphill throughout, giving a change in potential energy. Most candidates mistakenly invoked the principle of conservation of energy. This part requires a solution to a work/energy balance question. Parts (ii) and (iii) are more difficult exercises on problem solving. Answers: (i) Work done is 900 000 J or 900 kJ; (iii) Ratio is 0.75
notes.7: Some candidates were able to answer part (i). Part (ii) was more of a challenge. Part (iii) was the best answered part of this question. Most candidates were challenged to develop a strategy for solving the problem in part (iv). Answers: (ii) 16.9 ms-1 (or 16 7/8 ms-1); (iii) 1070 m; (iv) t = 144 seconds
notes.key_messages:
• It is important for candidates to read the questions carefully, and answer as required.
• Candidates need to take care to avoid arithmetic and sign errors.
notes.general_comments:
This paper requires some answers derived from just the use of basic ideas and some answers derived from
the use of basic ideas in the context of problem solving. Even questions focusing on basic ideas proved
challenging for some candidates.
